standard.title: Deliver short spoken texts
standard.description: create and deliver short spoken texts to report ideas and events to peers, using features of voice such as appropriate volume
standard.prior_knowledge: Students interact orally in informal settings. They have not yet been asked to prepare and deliver a deliberately constructed spoken text to an audience of peers — with conscious attention to voice features such as volume.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can create and deliver a short spoken text to peers — reporting an idea or event — using appropriate volume and staying on topic.

nodes.label: A spoken text has a topic
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the topic they want to talk about and share at least one idea or event related to it.
nodes.minimum_width: Name what their spoken text will be about and share one idea or fact.
nodes.typical_width: Share a personal experience, interest or discovery with peers; stay on the topic selected; sequence ideas or events with support from visual prompts.
wider: Share spoken texts on topics from different areas — personal experience, a book shared in class, something learned in another subject
Compare what is easy to share orally versus in writing — identifying what each mode does well
nodes.hinge_reason: Without identifying a topic and having content to share, the audience-directed delivery in Node 2 has nothing to work with — volume adjustment and visual prompt use are tools for delivering content, not a substitute for it.

response_modes.reason: Topic focus and content generation must be reliable before students can attend to delivery features. Practice at identifying a topic and sharing ideas builds the foundation for Node 2 delivery.

success_criteria: Student's spoken text is identifiably about a topic.
Student shares at least one idea or event related to the topic.

nodes.label: Volume and focus for an audience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can adjust their volume for an audience of peers and use visual prompts to stay on topic.
nodes.minimum_width: Deliver a short spoken text at an audible volume to peers using at least one visual prompt.
nodes.typical_width: Use appropriate volume for a semi-formal peer audience; use visual prompts (objects, drawings, digital images) to stay on topic and sequence ideas.
wider: Deliver the same spoken text in different contexts — to one partner, to a small group, to the whole class — adapting volume accordingly
Create and use visual prompts for a spoken text — selecting images or drawings that sequence ideas effectively
Deliver a short response to a First Nations Australian story or cultural account with attention to appropriate ways of sharing

response_modes.reason: Audience-directed delivery requires integrating topic focus, volume control, and use of visual supports simultaneously. These skills were practised separately; here they must work together in performance.

success_criteria: Student can be heard clearly by peers without shouting.
Student stays on topic with or without visual prompts.
Student delivers a text of at least two to three connected ideas or events.
